rules.rationale: High heteroatom density increases hydrogen bonding and aqueous stabilization, raising desolvation cost and suppressing measured lipophilicity.
Extended pi surface with only moderate polarity gives large nonpolar contact area; mechanistically meaningful two-condition interaction for octanol partitioning.
Moderate halogen substitution raises polarizability and hydrophobic surface; halogen_mid (743) is far better supported than sparse halogen_high (98).
Counter-hypothesis downweighting the low-confidence (0.224) length transfer: extreme-length molecules often carry polar solubilizing groups, not bulk hydrophobicity.

skill.hypothesis: Domain-knowledge counter-view: polarity penalty plus aromatic and halogen hydrophobic surface drives lipophilicity, and the uncertain length relation reverses at extreme lengths. Fails if bulk molecular size dominates partitioning in this pool.
